title: 3Sum
description: Find all unique triplets in the array which sum to zero.
pseudocode:
1. Sort(nums)
2. For i from 0 to n-3:
3.   If i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1] continue
4.   left = i + 1, right = n - 1
5.   While left < right:
6.     sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]
7.     If sum == 0: add triplet, increment left, decrement right
8.     Else if sum < 0: increment left
9.     Else: decrement right

steps.note: Sort the input array to enable two-pointer approach.
Starting main loop at i=0, nums[i]=-4.
Calculate sum: -4 + -1 + 2 = -3. Sum < 0, move left pointer.

fullDescription:
Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.

Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.

 

Example 1:

Input: nums = [-1,0,1,2,-1,-4]
Output: [[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]]
Explanation: 
nums[0] + nums[1] + nums[2] = (-1) + 0 + 1 = 0.
nums[1] + nums[2] + nums[4] = 0 + 1 + (-1) = 0.
nums[0] + nums[3] + nums[4] = (-1) + 2 + (-1) = 0.
The distinct triplets are [-1,0,1] and [-1,-1,2].
Notice that the order of the output and the order of the triplets does not matter.

Example 2:

Input: nums = [0,1,1]
Output: []
Explanation: The only possible triplet does not sum up to 0.

Example 3:

Input: nums = [0,0,0]
Output: [[0,0,0]]
Explanation: The only possible triplet sums up to 0.

 

Constraints:

  • 3 <= nums.length <= 3000
  • -105 <= nums[i] <= 105
